children: Copper stocks plunge pre-market Thursday following a Reuters report that the White House has not ​yet made a decision on refined copper tariffs, as the Trump administration weighs concerns of higher prices that could raise manufacturing costs against the potential benefits of encouraging more domestic mining.
Among relevant stocks in pre-market trading: Freeport-McMoRan
In Europe, miners are the worst performing sector, including Antofagasta

Copper futures prices have steadily climbed toward $15K/ton, on track for an 11th consecutive weekly gain on the London Metal Exchange, sparked largely by the shift of hundreds of thousands of tons to U.S. warehouses, which has tightened supplies elsewhere.

"We highlight the risk of a bubble," Natixis analyst Bernard Dahdah said in a note. "Prices are currently being driven by U.S. import arbitrage opportunities and fast money, rather than fundamentals and end-consumer demand."
If the Trump administration decided against placing import tariffs on refined metal, "then the arbitrage closes," Dahdah wrote. "Outflows from the U.S. could put large pressure on LME prices."

If tariffs are imposed as expected—at 15% for 2027 followed by a 30% rate for 2028, according to Dahdah—"then the arbitrage window also closes and U.S. imports collapse (as in-land material is consumed)," he added.

title: Copper stocks slump as White House tariff plan reportedly stalls
